Task: task_7
Description: Infer a full resistor network consistent with the effective-resistance measurements. Resistances are in ohms.

Required submission format:
JSON string with circuit topology (e.g., {"resistors": {"R1": x, ...}, "connections": [["A","B","R1"], ...]})

It is connected, with no self-loops or parallel edges.', 'Measurements are rounded to 3 decimal places. Any node pair may have a resistor; resistor IDs are arbitrary.', 'Submit all resistors and nodes. Any circuit satisfying these constraints and matching EVERY supplied effective resistance within 0.000500001 ohms is accepted.', 'Each resistor must have a value from this list (ohms): [10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 28, 31, 35, 38, 42, 47, 52, 58, 64, 71, 79, 88, 97, 108, 119, 132, 147, 163, 180, 200]. Values may repeat; no per-value inventory is provided.']

IMPORTANT: You have access to filesystem tools. Use only canonical absolute paths under `/workspace`; relative paths and other absolute roots are rejected.

I found a 23-resistor network that matches all 35 measurements within the 0.0005 Ω tolerance, and the submission was accepted.

**How I found it:** I started from a fit with every possible node pair connected, then removed the weakest resistors one at a time until 23 were left. After that I kept swapping single resistors in and out until the fit was essentially exact. Every fitted value came out very close to a value on the allowed list, so I rounded each one to its nearest allowed value. I checked the rounded network locally: its largest error against the measurements is 0.00047 Ω.

**What didn't work:**
- **Random search alone:** trying random layouts and allowed values directly never got close enough.
- **Measured pairs only:** connecting resistors only between pairs that were actually measured couldn't fit the data, so some resistors are between pairs that weren't measured.
